name: ActorActionSeq_CollectPendingNodeIds
summary: Collects the ids of enabled-but-not-yet-started nodes of an action-sequence node array (0x10-byte nodes, flag byte +9 set, state byte +0xC clear) into a 50-entry stack buffer and asks the data panel to reset the rows with those ids; returns the count.
evidence: Sibling 0x003BDF58 walks the very same array with the complementary filter (+0xC == 1) and both feed the ids to the list-data table (g_uiListData+0x6B8 / Ui_DataPanel_ResetRowsByIndexList on bag work), so these are action-sequence node ids consumed as list-row keys. Callers Ui_Window_StartAction17Or12 and Ui_Window_InputToState11Or6 use it as the window helper that clears the rows of nodes that have not started; the stored value is an id, not a node, so the old name was one noun too vague.

name: ActorActionSeq_CollectStartedNodeIds
summary: Complement of 0x003BDE6C: collects the ids of the action-sequence nodes whose flag byte +9 is set and whose state byte +0xC equals 1 (already started) into a 0x50-byte buffer and hands them to the slot-table compactor; returns the count.
evidence: Identical loop over the same 0x10-byte node array as 0x003BDE6C, only the +0xC test flipped; the callee 0x0018D3D4 is called with g_uiListData+0x6B8 and the id list, and its neighbour 0x0018D380 removes one entry of a 19x0x98 list-data table. The ids are therefore list-data/sequence row ids, not party member ids as the old name claimed.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_ActionEntryTail
summary: Cold tail block of the battle action-entry builder 0x003C3F5C (no prologue, live r4-r8): for each of the six action slots it stores the resolved actor into the entry at +0x12BC, the validity byte at +0x12C2 and copies the 0x58-byte target record at +0x1264, spawning a balloon through Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor when the battle 3D flag (+0x4244) is set.
evidence: Disassembly starts with bl Os_GetGameWork and no push frame and the pop is at 0x003C4A54, so this is a mid-function split symbol of 0x003C3F5C, not a callable routine; the stores it performs (actor pointer, validity byte, 0x58-byte record copy) are the only verified facts, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloonForSlot
summary: 32-byte per-slot balloon helper: when the sequence record byte +0x2A6 is clear it refreshes the balloon layout, otherwise it takes the member-anchored variant; in both cases it creates the effect instance for the balloon record id at +0x2BA and stores it at context+0xD8EC.
evidence: The two branches and the final Effect_FindOrCreateInstance(battle 2D/3D effect manager, record->u16_2BA, 0, ...) stored at self+0xD8EC are clear, but the body is a damaged decompilation using unaff_r4/unaff_r5, so the class and the word balloon stay unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemList_SelectItem
signature: void maybe_Ui_ItemList_SelectItem(void* itemList, u32 list, char* names)
summary: Item-list selection step: writes the newly chosen row into the list object, refreshes the category caption and the scroll, and formats the item name into a message argument; ends by resetting the UI core selection field.
evidence: The trustworthy part is the named callee set: Item_LookupRecord plus Text_FormatMessageArg/Message_SetArg pick and format an item name, Ui_Menu_SetCategoryText/Ui_ListWidget_ResetToFirstEntry/Ui_ListWidget_UpdateScroll refresh the list. The index arithmetic is still garbled (unaff_ registers, nonsense magic-multiply), so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_SelectMemberGauge
summary: 24-byte entry that calls the party-panel constructor 0x00325500 and then falls through into the shared 31-member scan that binds the HP gauge window to the party member of the currently selected row.
evidence: The whole routine is one bl to the ctor (0x00325500, also used by Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel) followed by the gauge-binding loop, so it is either a create-instance wrapper or a mid-function split; no caller and no vtable slot distinguishes the two, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_RebuildSprite
summary: Rebuild path of a 2D object sprite: releases the old sprite handle through the 2D effect manager, rebuilds the footprint rect and re-registers the sprite as a child of the actor.
evidence: Only Gfx_Sprite_BuildFootprintRect and Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild are trustworthy; the control flow hits halt_baddata and software_interrupt(0x24) and uses unaff_r4, so the sprite family is right but the rebuild role is not verifiable.

name: maybe_Effect_ParticleEmitter_InitPoolD
summary: Child-pool factory of one effect-node class: allocates a 0xAC-byte node with the emitter allocator, installs the vtable <poolD>, stores the parent emitter at +0x20 and default-constructs two 0x40-byte sub-objects; on allocation failure it re-seeds the shared default animation block and clears the parent pool pointer.
evidence: Same allocate-copy-or-default template as 0x004721C4/0x004B143C/0x004721C4 family, all with a 64-entry two-word pool built by std_ConstructArray(obj+9, ctor, 0x40, 2); the object is a sequence/pool node rather than necessarily a particle emitter, and there are no callers, so the class noun stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectNodeCreateChild_75B164
summary: Child-object factory of the second effect/scene node class (vtable 0x75B164): allocates a 0xAC-byte child, initialises the member pair with the child vtable and the parent back-pointer, and constructs two 0x40-byte sub-objects; falls back to the default block when the allocation fails.
evidence: Identical template to 0x0044EC8C (same Mem_AllocAligned_2(0xAC) + Ui_Object_InitMemberPair + std_ConstructArray pair) with the other vtable; the class behind 0x75B164 is still unidentified and there are no callers, so only the vtable address identifies it.

name: maybe_Ui_OverlaySlot_CreateSpriteWithArgs
summary: Creates the 200x120 sprite mesh of a UI overlay slot from the resource string s_sprite_0061A940, installs it on the object and registers it with the sprite-actor layer.
evidence: Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance and Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh are confident callees and the mesh size constants (200 x 0x78) are explicit, so the sprite-mesh creation is certain; the owning overlay-slot class is only inferred and the function has no callers, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ProfileScreen_UpdateSelection
summary: Update step of a list window driven by the controller at window+0x11C: after a 0.25f delay it either activates the cursor row or pushes controller state 4, 5 or 8 depending on the pause flag and the root mode, then runs the controller.
evidence: The controller state ids 4/5/8, the Party_GetFirstNameLength guard and Ui_ListWindow_ActivateCursorRow are clear, but there are no callers and nothing names the window itself, so the ProfileScreen noun stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ProfileScreen_ConfirmSelection
summary: Confirm step of the same window as 0x00466350: when the root singleton is idle it resets the save-work transform and either activates the cursor row or advances the shared controller to state 9.
evidence: Shares the controller at window+0x11C and the pendingSelection field with 0x00466350, so the update/confirm pairing is solid; the window class is still unnamed and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_BuildSlotIds
summary: Large gimmick slot-setup routine: only the std_ConstructArray of eight 4-byte slot entries survives in the decompilation, the rest of the 1408-byte body is unreachable, so what ids are built cannot be read back.
evidence: Callers Field_Gimmick_BuildPartSlots, Field_Gimmick_ApplyConfigBlock and Field_Gimmick_InitSlotIds place it in gimmick slot setup and the eight 4-byte array is visible, but Ghidra ends the body at std_ConstructArray (marked noreturn), so the name stays maybe_.

name: Svc_AcClient_CloseIfSessionOpen
summary: Closes the AC (friend/network) session if one is still open: checks Svc_AcClient_CheckSession and calls Svc_AcClient_Close when it reports a session, returning the status.
evidence: The 24-byte entry is exactly push {r4,lr}; bl Svc_AcClient_CheckSession; cmp; blne Svc_AcClient_Close; pop, and 0x00501D14 is a separate entry that owns the monitor/refcount teardown Ghidra appended here. So the routine neither acquires nor locks anything - the old AcquireSessionLock name described the neighbouring function. Callers Ui_PresentMessage_Manager_Reset and Ui_ShutdownCommonResources use it as the session release.

name: maybe_Text_BuildGlyphQuadsThumb
signature: void maybe_Text_BuildGlyphQuadsThumb(int self, u32 count, float * chars, float * layout)
summary: Thumb fragment of the glyph-quad builder 0x0055B984: the same per-character transform/UV loop, appearing both as its caller and as its callee, so it is a mid-function split symbol rather than an independent routine.
evidence: 0x0055B984 Text_BuildGlyphQuads is listed both as the only caller and as a callee, and the body is damaged (unaff_r6/unaff_r7, BADSPACEBASE, coprocessor move), which is the signature of a split symbol; no item lookups appear, this is not item code.

name: maybe_Effect_SpawnOrientedInstance
summary: Spawns an effect instance oriented by a model node: builds the transform from the parent model node (Model_GetNodeIdByName plus the node matrix) or from the parent's rotation, applies the record's own offset/rotation, and finally calls Effect_FindOrCreateInstance with the record id at +0x3A.
evidence: The tail call Effect_FindOrCreateInstance(g_effectManager, arg2->u16_3A, 0, &transform) and the Model_GetNodeIdByName / Math_BuildQuaternionFromEuler transform assembly are unambiguous, but the decompilation is damaged (unaff_r6/r9/r10/r11, in_cr7, coprocessor_store) and the entry has no caller list, so confidence stays below 0.5.

name: maybe_BattleScene_CountVisibleUnits
summary: Counts the visible entries of the first battle unit list (battle work +0x4254) through Container_List_CountVisible; the rest of the body is lost to a bad-instruction truncation.
evidence: Only the Container_List_CountVisible call on battle+0x4254 (per FACTS the first unit list) is recoverable and the body ends in halt_baddata, so what the count is used for - and whether it is even returned - cannot be checked.

name: HandleRecord_GetNameLength
summary: Returns the length of the wide name at rec+8 when the record's four leading id bytes are all set (none 0xFF) and 0 otherwise: a validity-gated name-length getter for handle records.
evidence: The 0x00100B32 Str_WcsStr tail is a wcslen (loop over u16 until 0, then return), and the eight callers (Anim_SaveStateToSlot, Ui_Marker_FollowActor, Field_Actor_ApplySchedule, Ui_DiveCapture_*) all measure the name of a record whose 4-byte id is 0xFFFFFFFF when unused. It returns a value, so a Get* name is correct.

name: maybe_Monster_CountDistinctRecordedKinds
summary: Builds a 65-word bitmask over the kind byte +0x22 of every id present in owner+0x3AE4 (plus the three related ids reached through the variant offset table), popcounts it and returns the number clamped to 999.
evidence: Mechanics are intact (loop bound 0x413, Data_LookupSubRecord accessor, popcount, clamp 0x3E7) but the callers are Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats and Menu_StatusScreen_InitFaceAndCommands, which do not fit a monster walk, and the record accessor 0x0063DCA4 has no readable file, so the table identity and the meaning of +0x22 stay open.

name: maybe_Monster_SumRecordedCounts
summary: Walks the 0x413 ids, adds the per-id u32 counter at owner+0x3AE4 for every record whose kind byte +0x22 is non-zero and returns the total clamped to 99,999.
evidence: The summation and the 0x1869F clamp are fully readable, but the same caller mismatch as 0x0062A4BC applies (Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats / Menu_StatusScreen_InitFaceAndCommands) and accessor 0x0063DCA4 is unnamed, so neither the table nor the counter meaning is proven.

name: maybe_Ui_BagCategory_FilterAvailable
signature: void maybe_Ui_BagCategory_FilterAvailable(u32* out, BagListOwner* owner, int category)
summary: Builds the 7-byte row list of a list owner, keeps only the ids whose category membership test 0x003AA574 succeeds, and packs them into the 0xFF-prefilled output.
evidence: New context: callers Ui_PlateWidget_BindEntry and Ui_ItemRows_RefreshRows use it to fill a 7-row plate/list from the owner's slot list, and the membership test is the same 0x003AA574 as before - but that callee is itself only maybe_ named (SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill), so the category reading stays tentative.

name: maybe_DataTable_IsIndexValidB
summary: Range guard of a data-table row: when the row's style byte at +0 is below 0x1F it resolves the table header and answers with the sub-index test against the header limit at +8; otherwise it answers 1.
evidence: Header getter 0x0063F93C is a mid-function label inside Ui_ListRow_SumRowHeights and the four callers (Party_GetActorNoForCharacter, Party_BuildUsedCharacterList, Party_FindEntryByType, Battle_Group_BuildFromString_Tail) never name the table, so the identity stays open. Note the comparison reads inverted relative to the name: it returns 0 when the sub-index is inside the header limit, which is one more reason to keep maybe_.

name: DataTable_GetEntryB
summary: Resolves the table header, follows its +0xC relative section pointer and returns the 5-byte entry selected by the sub-index at plate+0x10.
evidence: Exactly the header accessor + relative +0xC section + 5-byte stride the four Party_* callers need to index their table, and the body writes nothing, so a Get* name is right; the only doubt is the wording DataTable, which is deliberately generic because the table itself is unnamed.

name: Field_CheckGridInteraction
summary: Player interaction probe: resolves the grid cell under the player, classifies the four neighbouring direction entries (g_fieldGridInteractionMaskTable) against the map-object tables and confirms the hit with the point test 0x00651954.
evidence: Named caller Field_TryPlayerInteract uses it as the grid-cell probe before starting the interaction and the second caller is the gated variant; the four-direction loop over g_fieldGridInteractionMaskTable plus func_0062C23C(manager, entry, direction, mask) is explicit, so the interaction-grid reading holds.

name: Field2D_Layer_GetField12
summary: Returns byte +0x12 of the active 2D map-layer record (layer->f_04->f_298); callers compare it against walk-trigger and collision state, but which layer attribute the byte is (id, floor or tag) is not proven, hence the offset-based name.
evidence: Disassembly is a pure three-load getter (ldr r0,[r0,#4]; ldr r0,[r0,#0x298]; ldrb r0,[r0,#0x12]) and all four callers are named Field2D_* functions of the map/scene layer code (MapChip_ResetWalkTrigger, Actor_CheckCollisionBox, Scene_BuildFromMapData, Scene_UpdateLayers), so the getter shape and the Field2D family are certain.

name: maybe_Engine_SubmitFrameEntries
summary: Engine frame step: pumps the sound voice list and, when global 0x007AE18C is set, calls vtable +0x20 on every object of the self->f_54..f_58 array with fixed frame arguments (0x3F, args, 0x100, 10).
evidence: The only caller is Engine_Initialize, which does not fit a per-frame submit, and the queued object class is unidentified; the indirect vtable+0x20 loop and the sound pump are all that is verified, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields(void* self, u32 transferSource, u32 eventArg, u32 eventArg2)
summary: Initialises one asynchronous transfer channel: stores the source pointer, initialises the completion event, points the callback at the channel and submits a 0x2000-byte staging buffer (mode 0x11, handle -2); returns 1.
evidence: Body is fully readable (pointer, Os_LightEvent_Init, Gfx_CommandBuffer_Submit(&cmd, src, 0x2000, 0x11, -2)) and both callers are engine startup (Engine_Initialize, InitHeaps), so it is an engine-level transfer slot; the Fs_Channel noun remains a guess because no Fs service is opened.

name: Field_SceneNode_UpdateExtentAndTrail
summary: Per-step update of a scene-node action: mode 1 interpolates the node extents (f_98/f_9C) with rounding, mode 2 pushes a trail sample via Gfx_Trail_PushSample, and a sub-mode plays an animation on the target node.
evidence: All the work in the body is done by named callees: Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation, Gfx_Trail_PushSample, Gfx_Trail_TryConnectCell and std_Expf, and the three action states map one-to-one onto extents / trail / animation, so the descriptive name holds even though the class behind the action object is unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_StepLayout
summary: Per-frame driver of a timed text layout: interpolates the text origin over a 0x10-frame window, binds the style resources of the first 0x18-byte part entry and spawns effects/sounds per part.
evidence: Callees maybe_Ui_TextBuilder_SetStyleResource, Ui_SmithMenu_SetParamValue and the 0x18-byte per-part loop are clear, but the only caller is Ui_ListWindow_DispatchInput and several callee names are themselves only maybe_ / misnomers, so the owning class stays open.

name: Field_NpcAction_PlayScaledActionAnim
summary: Starts an NPC action step: reads the action animation id and the actor move speed, installs one of the two animation name pointers (0x0032FE78 / 0x0032FE7C) through the actor vtable slot +0x84 and applies a randomised system-speed value when the actor animation is ready.
evidence: Field_NpcGetActionAnimId and Field_Actor_GetMoveSpeedAndFlag are named callees and the 0x0032FE7C callback is the same step word installed by its twins 0x0033026C and 0x0033045C, so the NPC action-step role is established; only the scaled-anim wording remains inferred from the anim-id/flag pair.

name: maybe_Ui_WindowWithList_Ctor
summary: Constructs the list window embedded in the dive window: base ctor with vtable 0x2CFACC, an embedded scroller at +0x54 with eight rows and a 0x3C x 8 array of row records.
evidence: Only caller Ui_DiveWindow_Ctor and the vtable 0x2CFACC are certain; the 8x0x3C row array and the scroller match the Ui_*_ListWindow family (Ui_PagedTextListWindow_Ctor already exists as a different constructor), so a generic WindowWithList name is the honest description.

name: Field_CreateSpriteObject
summary: Allocates an object from the field object pool (0x0017C1C8) and installs g_gfxSpriteObjectVtable, i.e. creates a plain field sprite object.
evidence: The 24-byte body is only the pool allocation plus the vtable stamp of g_gfxSpriteObjectVtable, and the named caller Field_CreateActorData calls it to give the actor its sprite; nothing implements interaction, so the old Interactable noun was too specific and belonged to the caller.

name: Field_InteractJob_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the field interaction job node: allocates from the field pool, installs g_fieldInteractJobVtable and sets the state bytes +0x45 = 1 and +0x46 = 0xFF.
evidence: The installed global is g_fieldInteractJobVtable and the caller is Field_SceneObjectCtor_vt23EC5C, which builds the field scene object that owns the job; the two initialised state bytes are the only other content, so the constructor reading is safe.

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenChild_Ctor_77E254
summary: Constructor of one of the fifteen child objects built by Ui_ScreenController_InitChildren: chains Ui_MotionPath_Ctor, installs vtable 0x0077E254, clears ~0x38 state words and chains four 0x004B65C0 sub-objects.
evidence: Vtable 0x0077E254 shares Camera_Field_Delete (+0x04) and Camera_Field_Update (+0x10) with the field-camera vtable 0x0077E258, so the object is camera-related, but the exact child class is unresolved and there are no strings; the vtable address stays in the name.

name: maybe_Os_FlushDspServiceCommand
summary: Flushes one pending DSP-service command: drains the eight event handles, waits on g_dspServiceMutex, dispatches the queued Gfx_IpcCmd120000 request, clears the pending byte, signals the semaphore and marks the service state byte +3.
evidence: The body is a complete state machine over g_dspServiceState/g_dspEventHandles and ends with Gfx_IpcCmd120000(state[8]) - it dispatches a queued command rather than waiting on a sync object, so the old WaitSyncObject name described the mutex wait only. Its only caller is Os_ShutdownSyncPrimitives; the exact caller-side contract is still unverified, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_StartGpuWorkerThread
signature: void maybe_Gfx_StartGpuWorkerThread(u32 namePtr, int handleA, int handleB)
summary: Installs the caller's two shared-memory handles plus a freshly created kernel object into g_gpuSessionHandles, initialises the sync event and starts the GPU worker thread on it.
evidence: Caller Mem_MapSharedBlock is what supplies handleA/handleB (so this is the handle-registration + thread start for the mapped GPU block) and Os_CreateThreadWithStack/Os_LightEvent_Init are named, but the thread procedure and the session semantics are still unverified.

name: maybe_Snd_ProcessPendingStreams
summary: Completes a pending CSND transfer: signals the transfer completion event, marks the transfer and channel state bytes and tears the stream context down through 0x001132DC.
evidence: Readable body over g_csndTransferActive/g_csndChannelParamBlock; the teardown callee is itself only maybe_ named (maybe_Snd_TeardownStreamContext) and there are no callers, so the stream noun is unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Svc_DispatchTwoRecordRequest
summary: Builds a two-entry 0x10-byte-stride request array with std_ConstructArray and dispatches it with the caller's request word.
evidence: The only visible statement is std_ConstructArray(requestArray, 0x00119838, 0x10, 2) - Ghidra treats ConstructArray as noreturn and drops the dispatch, so the request/response halves come from the disassembly note only; the only caller is Svc_RequestWithRetry.

name: maybe_Snd_CalcVolumePan
summary: Per-voice sound state update: reads the voice state through its vtable, queues the follow-up command (Snd_QueueCommandBuffer(...,5)) and, for the 3D-position branch, computes two short values from the squared distance terms and stores them through two pointers - i.e. the volume/pan pair of the voice.
evidence: The function ends with *outA = (short)sqrt-term; *outB = (short)sqrt-term after a table of squared distances, which fits an attenuation/pan computation, and the Snd_QueueCommandBuffer call fixes the sound family; but the body is damaged (unaff_r6/r9/r10/r11, in_cr7, coprocessor_store) so the maths cannot be verified.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PushUnitRandomIds
summary: For every unit of the battle party list: resolves its party record, rolls one random id per each of four min/max byte pairs at record+0x370 with the battle RNG and pushes each non-zero id to the unit widget's vtable +0x40, then pushes the record's +0x398 value as a final id.
evidence: Readable body: func_001CA474(battleRng_4218, pair[0], pair[1], 0) per pair plus the f_398 value, all pushed through slot +0x40 of the unit widget; the only caller is Battle_UpdateUnitCommandPhase. Nothing here formats or applies message text, so the old ApplyUnitMessageText wording named the wrong effect - which ids are rolled (voice/pose/message set) is still open.

name: maybe_Text_ConstructRowTable
summary: Builds the six-word metric table used by 0x0039CBBC (std_ConstructArray of 6 four-byte entries) and reads the game work first when the alternate flag is clear.
evidence: Body is reduced to one std_ConstructArray(elementArray, 0x005F9720, 4, 6) plus a Game_GetWork call, so the row/column meaning is inferred from its caller. Note the caller 0x0039CBBC is itself called from 0x001D5098 whose five callers are all *InterpolateOwnerVector helpers, so a maths/metric role is as likely as a text role - the Text_ prefix is doubtful, which is why the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_Layout_SetLineLimit
signature: void maybe_Text_Layout_SetLineLimit(uint8_t* lineCount, TextLayout* layout, uint32_t lineLimit)
summary: Stores the line budget at layout+0x4C and returns when the line counter already reached it or exceeds 3; otherwise it appends the next 5-word record (std_ConstructArray of 0x005F9720 elements).
evidence: The counter/limit compare is readable but the tail is a lost std_ConstructArray, and the same caller chain as 0x0039CA80 (0x0039CBBC, reached only from the *InterpolateOwnerVector helpers) makes the text-line reading doubtful; keep maybe_ until 0x0039CBBC itself is resolved.

name: maybe_Math_Vector3_Interpolate
signature: void maybe_Math_Vector3_Interpolate(float* arg1, float* from, float* out, uint32_t mode)
summary: Adapter that builds a 3-word record from its third argument (func_0039CD08) and forwards it with the second argument and the mode word to 0x0039CBBC; the first argument is never read.
evidence: All five callers (Battle_Unit_ApplyModelParts and four maybe_Field_InterpolateOwnerVector* helpers) pass (manager, from, outVector, mode) and the helper is slot 13 of a 24-slot vtable, which supports a vector interpolation; but its only callee 0x0039CBBC is currently named Text_LayoutSingleLine (0.55), and one of the two readings must be wrong, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_Ctor_vt759F88
summary: Constructor of a window-like object: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x00759F88, seeds state bytes/vectors and a 0.3f scale, then chains a sub-object, a Ui_SlotTable and a third helper.
evidence: The named callees are Ui_WindowState_Init and Ui_SlotTable_Ctor (plus maybe_Ui_SlotTable_InitSubParts), i.e. the object owns a window state and a slot table, so a Field_ object is very unlikely - the old Field_ObjectCtor prefix named the wrong subsystem. The owner of vtable 0x00759F88 is still unknown and there are no callers, so the generic Ui_Window noun and maybe_ stay.

name: maybe_Menu_RemoveActorAttachments
summary: Walks the battle party list and the four 0x1C-stride unit lists: for every actor carrying a tag at +0x8EC it calls vtable +0xE4(actor, tag, 1), and when the monster record value at +0x103 is at least the RNG roll (1..100) it also calls vtable +0x50(actor, 1, 0).
evidence: The tag compare, the +0xE4 virtual call and the RNG-gated +0x50 call are readable, and the only caller is Menu_ApplySelectedCharacter; but which two actor states those vtable slots toggle (visibility? condition? attachment?) is not visible anywhere, so the attachments noun stays a guess.

name: Menu_ClaimFreeSlotForId
signature: void Menu_ClaimFreeSlotForId(void* self, u32 id, u32 arg3, u32 stack)
summary: Claims a free record of the five 0x40-byte slots at self+0x4C..+0x14C: returns immediately when the id is already present, otherwise stamps u16 id at +0x0E of the first record whose bytes +0x0C/+0x0D are -1 and whose id is 0xFFFF, clears +0x08, sets +0x10 = -1 and refreshes the entry icon.
evidence: Named caller BattlePartyWindow_ClaimPartySlots and the five-slot membership scan fix the claim-a-free-slot role, and maybe_Menu_UpdateItemIcon is called right after the stamp; what is still open is only whether the ids are party members or item entries, which the neutral name does not claim.

name: Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RefreshMemberSlots
summary: Walks the battle party list at battleWork+0x4260 and, for each living unit, passes its three u8 ids at +0xB115/+0xB135/+0xB155 to Menu_Slot_StoreActorId when the resolved character record has the +0x2F2 flag set.
evidence: The only caller is the confidently named Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RefreshMembers, the callee is Menu_Slot_StoreActorId, and the three ids are resolved through the named CharacterRecord wrapper 0x0018C184 before the +0x2F2 gate - the slot-refresh role is therefore established.

name: Ui_CharaStatusWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the character-status window object: allocates through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs g_uiCharaStatusWindowVtable, sets the +0x49 sentinel to 0xFF and constructs the embedded part plus two Ui_AnimRefList lists, returning the embedded part pointer.
evidence: Three independent facts agree: the installed global is g_uiCharaStatusWindowVtable, the function sits 0x3C bytes before Ui_CharaStatusWindow_Dtor (0x002590DC) in the same class block (FillPartyMember / Release / BindCharaPanes / Update / DeletingDtor), and its only caller Ui_TsuyosaWindow_CreateInstance creates exactly such an embedded window. No other CharaStatusWindow ctor exists.

name: Field_BattleUnitObject_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the field object that owns battle-unit data: installs the class vtable, destroys the pack handle, destroys three 0xDC-byte sub-records, re-installs g_battleUnitObjectVtable on the base, runs the base destructor and frees the block.
evidence: The base object is explicitly stamped with g_battleUnitObjectVtable and the teardown (Pack_Handle_Dtor, std_destroy_range of three 0xDC records, 0x00200220, operator delete) is the standard deleting-dtor shape, so both the class and the role are supported; the Field_ prefix stays because the vtable is the field-side wrapper.

name: FieldParty_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field-party object: installs the vtable, releases the pack handle at +0x125C, runs the base destructor 0x00200220 and frees; the non-freeing twin is 0x00265900.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionObject_DtorDelete

name: maybe_Battle_ActionObject_Dtor

name: maybe_Field_InteractiveObject_DtorB
summary: Deleting destructor template: installs the vtable, releases the packed handle at +0x497, runs the base destructor 0x00200220 on the adjusted pointer and frees.

name: maybe_FieldParty_DtorDelete

name: maybe_Field_ActorActionSeq_DeletingDtor

name: maybe_Battle_ActorAction_DeletingDtorA

name: maybe_Text_MessageWindow_Dtor
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: base destructor 0x00200220 and operator delete 0x0010F6CC on the message-window object.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PartyRowPanel_DeleteB
summary: Deleting destructor variant: stores the vtable, runs the base destructor 0x00200220 and operator delete.
