name: Ui_ActivateScriptedElement
summary: Activates the scripted element of a UI window: marks the action-sequence record as running (f_30), advances its action id from the panel state, dispatches the script state callback, sets the window's step flag and list counter, and finally selects the element's list entry.
evidence: Four of the window input handlers in this batch call it for their input bit 8 (0x00308548, 0x002FDA70, 0x002A5FD4, 0x00308264), and the body is readable: Script_DispatchStateCallback, Container_SetCountFromByteSize and Ui_List_SelectEntryById on the element's pane. That fixes both the family and the role; only the word element is generic.

name: Battle_AnimElement_PlayDefaultMotion
summary: Resolves the element's actor by handle, requires the state-2 query to be clear, asks for the actor's default motion id, verifies the actor can play it and starts it with a battle-RNG delay.
evidence: The body is a clean chain of named callees (Menu_FindActorByHandle, Actor_GetDefaultMotionId, the actor vtable +0xE8 state query and +0x84 motion check, then the playback with the battle RNG at +0x4218), so play-default-motion-with-jitter is established. Nothing in the body identifies state 2 as damage, so the old PlayDamageAnim claim was too specific and is dropped.

name: Battle_Unit_PlayStatePoseIfSet
summary: Resolves the unit's actor by handle, asks Battle_SelectPoseGroup which pose group applies and plays it only when the returned group is non-zero.
evidence: The three named callees in order (Menu_FindActorByHandle with the handle at element+4, Battle_SelectPoseGroup, then the pose play call) leave no room for another reading; the only uncertainty is which unit state reaches this variant, which the name does not claim.

name: maybe_Battle_Action_ReplayPoseOnTimer
summary: When the timer value returned by 0x00669D38 exceeds 1.0f it resolves the action's actor by handle and replays the pose group chosen by Battle_SelectPoseGroup.
evidence: The pose replay half is certain (Menu_FindActorByHandle + Battle_SelectPoseGroup + play), but the timer producer 0x00669D38 is unnamed and the float arrives in a partially recovered register, so nothing proves the action is an idle state - the old UpdateIdleState wording claimed that without evidence.

name: Battle_Unit_PlayStatePoseWhenFlagged
summary: When the element flag at +0x2C is set, or the actor passes the 0x00669DD4 ready check, it resolves the actor by handle and plays the pose group selected by Battle_SelectPoseGroup.
evidence: Same named callee triple as 0x002DB0B8 plus the explicit +0x2C flag test and the ready check; the gate is readable and the element family is the 0x3FBxxx animation-element block, so only the element noun stays generic.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_PlayStatePoseWithCtx
summary: Pose replay: when the unit's motion is done, it takes the lazily created shared UI context, resolves the actor by handle and replays the state pose group.
evidence: Body is the same as 0x003CE0E4 (template copy) and the replay sequence (Menu_FindActorByHandle, Battle_SelectPoseGroup, play) is clear, but the lazy 0x98-byte context allocation merged into the body (g_osGameWork + g_uiMessageWindowBaseVtable2) is unexplained and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_PlayStatePoseWithCtxB
summary: Second copy of 0x002DAC4C: when the unit's motion is done it takes the lazily created UI context, resolves the actor by handle and replays the state pose group.
evidence: Identical body to 0x002DAC4C with only the element offsets differing, so the two are template copies; that also means the WithCtx wording describes the shared body, not a verified distinction, and no caller exists.

name: maybe_Container_LinkByName
summary: Damaged container helper fragment: the code reads strlen/memcmp of a 32-byte name, walks the global handle table, compares a vtable class pointer and links the matching object into the intrusive list at +0x7C.
evidence: The entry point starts mid-function (code_r0x0030C6DC) with unaff_ registers and only ~0x84 bytes are attributable, so neither the container class nor the link role can be confirmed even though the handle-table walk and the 32-byte name compare are visible.

name: maybe_Pack_HandleTable_ReacquireHandle
summary: Re-registers an object's handle: when owner+0x2CC still validates against the global handle table it adds that handle to the pack manager's table through Pack_HandleTable_Add and stores the returned index byte at owner+0x2D0, returning 1 on success.
evidence: The body is only the handle-table validity probe plus Pack_HandleTable_Add(packManager_60, &owner->f_2CC) with the index stored at +0x2D0, so the mechanism is certain; the caller Menu_IconModelLoadTask_Update shows the object is a menu icon model, not a field object, so the old Field_HandleAcquire prefix named the wrong subsystem while the exact class remains open.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateGlyphStyle
summary: Picks the glyph/icon style of the current message line: from the speaker's character record it takes the equipped item id at inventory slot 1, maps the item record byte +0xC0 (or the action record byte +0xA8) to a style id, stores it in the per-window short table and rebuilds the affected glyph runs.
evidence: The item/character lookups (func_006292F0 = equipped item id, func_0063DF9C = item record, func_0035EB98 = party member) are used only to choose a style id that is then stored at window+0xDE44 and passed to the glyph-run rebuilders; this is portrait/style selection, not item code. The only caller 0x00320868 is itself maybe_ named, so the message-window class stays unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Field_NpcAction_StartStepTowardTarget
summary: Starts an NPC action step toward a target: resolves the target id directly or through Container_FindObjectByTypeId, converts its move speed into the step timer, installs the step callback 0x0032FE7C and applies a randomised speed when the actor animation is ready.
evidence: Both halves are readable (Container_FindObjectByTypeId for the target, Field_NpcAction_GetMoveSpeedById -> stepTimer, vtable +0x84 install of 0x0032FE7C); it never turns or rotates anything visible, so the old TurnToActor wording was a guess. Which action kind this starts is still open.

name: maybe_Field_NpcAction_StartStepNoTarget
summary: Twin of 0x0033026C without the target lookup: takes the move speed of the actor's own id (+0x258), stores it as the step timer, installs the step callback 0x0032FE7C and applies the converted system speed when the actor animation is ready.
evidence: The only difference to 0x0033026C is the missing Container_FindObjectByTypeId lookup (the id is read from the actor at +0x258); the installed step word and the speed conversion are identical, so it is a no-target variant. What the step then does (idle, walk, wait) is not visible, hence the neutral NoTarget wording instead of IdleB.

name: Field_Actor_ResetPoseState
summary: Resets a field actor's movement/hold state: sets the busy flag +0xA7, either seeds the counter +0xA8 from two state words or zeroes it and calls vtable +0x98, then clears the held and movement vectors to zero.
evidence: Body is complete and self-contained, and both callers are named (Party_Status_RequestFieldActorRefresh, Ui_Overlay_AddEntry) and call it immediately before adding an overlay / refreshing the model, which is exactly a motion-state reset.

name: maybe_Ui_DebugMenu_SetPageState
summary: Resets a paged UI scene: drives the UI core commands when mode != 2, lazily creates/zeroes the 0x21C-byte pack manager singleton, hands its anim state id to the scene-transition manager, starts the movie player and clears the page state and elapsed time of self.
evidence: The callee set (Ui_GetCore, Ui_GetSceneTransitionManager, Gfx_Movie_PlayByName, maybe_Ui_Anim_SetStateId) and the 0x21C pack singleton (the same one 0x00623914 creates) are clear, but nothing debug-specific appears and there are no callers, so the DebugMenu noun stays a guess.

name: Effect_SpriteEmitter_SetupA
summary: A-variant sprite-emitter setup: copies layer/scale/origin from the definition, sets the euler rotation, builds the type-2 child sprite descriptor, attaches it at f_278 and loads effect pack 0x4B5.
evidence: The child descriptor is created with childType = 2 and attached through Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC before Gfx_EffectPack_LoadById(.., 5, 0x4B5), i.e. it configures a sprite child of an effect emitter; the twin 0x0040D620 differs only in the variant byte, and the sibling SetupE in the same block is a sprite-emitter setup too. Nothing in the body is quad-specific, so QuadEmitter was the wrong noun.

name: Effect_SpriteEmitter_SetupB
summary: B-variant sprite-emitter setup: same as 0x0040D4F8 plus the extra definition word at +0x17 stored as an attribute parameter and the variant state byte 1.
evidence: Byte-for-byte the same body as 0x0040D4F8 apart from the variant flag/sub-id and the extra attrib word; the same Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC(childType 2) plus Gfx_EffectPack_LoadById(0x4B5) skeleton fixes the sprite-emitter role, while quad is unsupported.

name: Effect_SpriteEmitter_SetupE
summary: E-variant sprite-emitter setup: copies position and layer from the definition, adds one billboard child sprite (childType 1) and initialises the sub-object at +0x2C8 with the definition byte 4.
evidence: Only Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC and the 0x005921EC sub-object init are involved and the child descriptor is childType 1 with a single billboard - a sprite emitter. The lettered variant and the emitter class stay inferred, and the sole caller is the unnamed field spawn block.

name: maybe_Battle_CommandEntry_Build
summary: Builds or validates one battle command entry; the readable body is only a large stack frame plus a lost 4x8-byte array constructor, so the field logic is invisible.
evidence: Ghidra ends the body at std_ConstructArray(entryWorkBuffer, 0x005906C0, 8, 4), so nothing of the actual entry handling survives; the four callers (Battle_Action_UpdateTargetFromGrid, Battle_Command_ResolveVariantCode, Battle_CommandListWindow_IsCursorUsable, maybe_Battle_CommandList_CommitSelection) only place it in the command-list path.

name: Field_ObjectSprite_UpdatePoseRaycastB
signature: void Field_ObjectSprite_UpdatePoseRaycastB(void* outRecord, FieldPoseObject* object, float* rayStart, float* rayDir)
summary: Raycasts the sprite's pose against scene geometry and writes the resulting draw parameters: builds the pose position from the attach node, calls Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine for the first hit and fills the out record with the hit distance/colour data.
evidence: The named graphics callees (Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext, Gfx_Scene_FindEntriesAlongLine, Gfx_Scene_DrawSprite, Math_BuildBoundsFromSphereAndOffset) plus the two named callers (Model_AttachAccessoriesAndWeapons and 0x004DA790) fix the raycast-and-update-sprite role; the B suffix only marks the second of the two variants.

name: Ui_IconCache_StartService
summary: Starts the icon-cache service once: when the state block says opened-but-not-started it takes the icon-cache monitor, calls 0x0050F2A4(0), waits ~60 ms, marks started and unlocks.
evidence: Its only caller is the named Ui_IconCache_Open and every global it touches is the icon-cache service state (g_uiIconCacheMonitor / g_iconCacheService); the one-shot started flag makes the StartService wording exact.

name: Ui_IconCache_ReadPageEntries
signature: int Ui_IconCache_ReadPageEntries(Ui_IconCache* self, Ui_IconPage* page, int* outPtrs, u32 size, int pageIndex)
summary: Reads one icon-cache page: asks the object's +8 vtable for the page size (command 3 for page 0, 4 for page 1), allocates/locks the matching page buffer under the icon-atlas monitor, copies the page header, validates the entry tag and writes the entry pointers into outPtrs.
evidence: All four callers are named Ui_IconCache_* entry points (Open, RequestPage, WriteEntry, plus std_vprintf_core) and the body works entirely on the page-index-0/1 state block and the g_uiIconAtlasMonitor; the read-one-page role is unambiguous.

name: maybe_Battle2DUnit_ShowActionPopup
summary: Same body as 0x00590B28 with state constant 0x82 instead of 0x33: polls a virtual predicate, triggers motion 0x79 and pushes a popup descriptor (kind 6) to the battle message queue.
evidence: The message-queue push with kind 6, the motion id 0x79 and the 0x125C state word are readable, but there is no caller and the class is inferred only from the address range, so the Battle2DUnit noun stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_TrySpawnAttachedEffect
summary: Checks the gimmick's effect handle, resolves the owner actor and its offset/rotation from the record at +0xA8 and spawns the attached effect instance through Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.
evidence: Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and the owner-actor transform build are clear, but the 728-byte body is truncated and the three callers are gimmick ctor/init helpers, so what triggers the spawn (and whether it is attached or positioned) cannot be confirmed.

name: Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowAndStoreArgs
signature: void Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowAndStoreArgs(void* self, void* ctx, int* args)
summary: Places one gimmick list row at the owner actor's position offset by args[0] * -5.0, re-applies the row asset id from args byte 6, copies the 0x11-byte argument block into self+0x1A8..+0x1C0 and signals the state machine.
evidence: Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId, Ui_ObjectList_SwapOrder and std_memcpy are the only calls and the 0x11-byte argument block plus the position from 0x004A1E00 are explicit, so place-one-row-and-store-args is what the body does; only the caller list is empty.

name: Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetFromArgs
signature: void Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetFromArgs(void* self, int arg2, int* args)
summary: Wrapper: resolves the gimmick owner through self+0x154C, converts args[1] to float (result dropped by Ghidra) and forwards *args as the row asset id for row 0.
evidence: The only real statement is the named Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId(self, *args) call after the owner lookup, so the wrapper role is exact; the dropped float conversion is the only unexplained part.

name: Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowsAndStoreArgs
signature: void Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowsAndStoreArgs(void* self, void* arg2, int* args)
summary: Places two gimmick rows at the owner actor's current position (asset id args[5] at row 1, args[2] at row -1), stores the actor/handle pair at +0x2DC/+0x2E0 and signals the handle-linked state machine.
evidence: Two named Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId calls with the position taken from 0x004A1E00 and the stored pair at +0x2DC are explicit; the only genuinely unknown value is the +0x2D4 word handed to 0x005E5140.

name: maybe_Field_Object_IsStatusFull
summary: Compares a per-id cost against a party limit: takes party member 0 via func_0035EB98, adds 10.0 when the work flags at +0x8AB1/+0x8AB2 are set and answers whether (record f_C + record f_15) stays within that limit.
evidence: The visible part is a party-member/limit comparison reached from maybe_Item_CheckCraftRequirements, Field_Actor_ConsumeLandingAnimId and maybe_Text_ConstructRowTable, i.e. it looks like a cost-vs-limit test rather than a status test; the 828-byte body is truncated at std_ConstructArray and both other callers are maybe_, so neither the noun nor the returned meaning is proven.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_CreateSlot
summary: One-shot initialisation of the 0x21C-byte UI scene object: allocates/zeroes it, attaches the shader_bch resource, registers the script system objects, and skips the work while the loading screen is active.
evidence: The callees (Gfx_ResourceList_Attach, Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueB, Script_RegisterSystemObjects, Ui_LoadingScreen_IsActive) and the shared vtable 0x007829E0 with 0x0066D0D0 are clear, but the same 0x21C pack singleton is created here and in 0x003EB028 and there are no callers, so the CreateSlot wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Item_CheckCraftRequirements
signature: u32 maybe_Item_CheckCraftRequirements(u32 arg1, RecipeWork* recipe, u32 scratch, u32 scratch2)
summary: Checks the six 10-byte requirement rows of a recipe: returns 1 when the work bytes +0x2D549/+0x2D54A are clear, otherwise walks each non-empty row {u16 itemId, u8 min, u8 max, ...} and stops at the first row whose bounds or extra status check fails.
evidence: The 10-byte row layout and the item-id/quantity bound compares are explicit and it ends in maybe_Field_Object_IsStatusFull, but all three callers carry camera-style names (Field_Actor_UpdateCameraAndAnim, Camera_IsPlayerViewClear, maybe_Camera_TestPointOccluded) that do not fit crafting and are themselves unreliable, so the recipe noun stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_SetVariantCallbackB
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Map_SetVariantCallbackB(MapRoot* mapRoot, u32 arg2, MapOwner* owner, int mode, int apply)
summary: Variant switcher of a 2D map node: mode 0 replays the direction animation (or stores the mode byte in owner+0x3E0 for mode 1) and installs either the sprite-node callback descriptor {0x0070D2CC, 0x006720F4} or rebuilds the layer task with {0x0070D454, 0x0067121C} / {0x0070D49C, 0x006713B4}.
evidence: All callees are named Field2D_* routines and the three descriptor triples are explicit, but no caller exists and 0x0067121C is already named Field2D_Map_RebuildLayerTaskA, so the object being installed is that layer task rather than a verified move controller - the CallbackB wording stays.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_RebuildMoveController
summary: Rebuilds the controller at f_A0: when f_58 still points at the inline default (+0x50) it releases the old object and creates a new one from self+0x70 with the descriptor {0x0070D454, 0x0067121C, self}, otherwise it calls the sprite-node reset path.
evidence: The two branches and the descriptor are clear, but 0x0067121C is named Field2D_Map_RebuildLayerTaskA, so what is created is that layer task and the MoveController wording is unproven; the factory 0x005BE5A8 is unnamed and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollList_MoveCursorWithPage
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollList_MoveCursorWithPage(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int pageCount)
summary: Page-aware cursor mover of a scrolling list: adds the delta to the row index, wraps it against the item count and re-selects the entry (Ui_List_SelectEntryById) before refreshing the rows.
evidence: The body is truncated by halt_baddata, calls through address 0 and uses unaff_r6; only the row-index update and the wrap against the item count are readable. The two callers (Ui_JumonWindow_Update, Ui_SmithMenu_HandleMaterialList) are both scrolling material/spell lists, so the family is right but the page logic is not verifiable.

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollList_ScrollByAnimated
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollList_ScrollByAnimated(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int scroll)
summary: Animated scroll of a list pane: adds the delta to the scroll index, clamps it against the item count, recentres or re-selects the new entry and refreshes through the window's virtual +0x60.
evidence: Damaged decompilation (bad instruction data, indirect call through address 0, unaff_r6/unaff_r7); the only caller is Ui_EquipWindow_PushSelectPane, which fits a list-pane scroll, but none of the arithmetic survives.

name: Effect_FindPackInfoByName
signature: void* Effect_FindPackInfoByName(const Handle* handle, const char* name)
summary: Resolves an effect pack-info object by name: validates the container handle against the global handle table, walks the objects of the hard-coded g_effectPackInfoClassRecord class, compares the object's inline 0x40-byte name and returns the first match.
evidence: The target class is the constant g_effectPackInfoClassRecord (not a parameter) and both callers, Effect_SetupPackInfo and Gfx_Effect2D_AttachPackInfo, pass a pack-info file name, so this is the effect pack-info lookup, not generic container code. The name copy itself is damaged (unaff_r register holds the registry node), which does not affect the role.

name: maybe_Gfx_HandleVBlank
summary: Display/vblank event handler: takes the display lock, sends the request word, and when the frame-done bit 0x20 is clear re-arms the display state and submits a 0x1000-byte command block to the display-transfer service.
evidence: The send/unlock/submit sequence (Svc_SendRequestWord, Os_UnlockScheduler, Gfx_ServiceDisplayTransfer with 0x1000 bytes) is clear, but the entry guard is a damaged flag register (in_ZR) and there are no callers, so the vblank attribution stays maybe_.

name: Os_DspService_InvokeShutdownCallbacks
summary: Runs the eight registered shutdown hooks of g_dspShutdownCallbacks once and clears the initialised byte +2 of g_dspServiceState.
evidence: The table and the state block are the same g_dspShutdownCallbacks / g_dspServiceState used by 0x00107100, whose caller is Os_ShutdownSyncPrimitives, so this is the DSP service shutdown hook runner; both callers (Gfx_ServiceDisplayTransfer, maybe_Snd_InitStreamContext) use it as the teardown step. The old Os_CallFinalizers wording hid which service owns the table.

name: maybe_Snd_ShutdownEngine
signature: void maybe_Snd_ShutdownEngine(void* engine, u32 arg2, u32* mask, int count)
summary: Stops the sound engine: marks f_358/f_348, closes the session handle at f_344, releases the command buffer at f_340, then walks a caller-supplied voice bitmask and releases each set 0x1C-byte voice record at f_24 + i*0x1C.
evidence: The two halves (engine teardown and per-voice release from a bitmask) both look plausible, but the Thumb body has overlapping instructions and lost unaff_r5/r6/r8/r11, and its only caller Gfx_MapResourceFormat does not fit, so whole-engine shutdown versus per-call voice release cannot be decided.

name: maybe_Snd_StreamManager_ServiceSlots
signature: void maybe_Snd_StreamManager_ServiceSlots(void* streamManager, u32 arg2, int count)
summary: Services pending stream slots under the sound command-queue mutex: completes finished streams and releases their channels.
evidence: Caller Snd_StreamManager_Update and the callees (Os_MutexLock on g_soundCommandQueueMutex, Snd_ReleaseAllChannels, Fs_SubmitAsyncTransfer) fix the stream-manager family, but the body has damaged decompilation (software_interrupt 0x24/0x14, extraout_r1) and a second caller SaveWork_Container_BaseCtor that does not fit.

name: Gfx_CommandQueue_AcknowledgeSlot
summary: Acknowledgement of the current GPU command-queue slot: locks the queue manager, either clears f_12 or marks the current 0x1C-byte slot entry ready and sets f_18, then unlocks.
evidence: The body works entirely on g_gpuCommandQueueManager (f_a0/f_11/f_12/f_18 and the 0x1C-stride slot array) under the lock helpers, and the three callers (Gfx_Display_PresentFrame, Fs_FileJob_Update, Fs_FileJob_UpdateAlt) ack one slot per frame/job; nothing applet- or suspend-related is touched, so Applet_AckSuspendState named the wrong owner.

name: maybe_Os_SignalAndClose
summary: If the runtime object exists, wakes its waiting thread and sends the close/notify request; a teardown step shared by the graphics, file and sound shutdown paths.
evidence: Four named callers (Gfx_WaitFrameInterval, Gfx_InitializeContext, Svc_RequestWithRetry, Sound_Driver_Shutdown) use it as a teardown step and the callees include maybe_Svc_IpcCmd19 / maybe_Os_IpcStatusQuery, but both of those are themselves only maybe_ named, so what exactly is closed stays open.

name: maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry
signature: int maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry(u32 dst, u32* outLen, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Drives a stack provider object through command 0x45, creates a kernel handle, waits on it with svcWaitSynchronization1 and closes it, retrying up to three times before copying the payload to dst.
evidence: Fs_ReadRecordBlock, Os_HandleInit/Os_GetCurrentProcessHandle and the svc 0x23/0x24 wait-close loop are named, so the read-with-retry shape is right; the provider object and its vtable are unnamed and the only caller is maybe_Gfx_BlitWorker, so the Fs_ subsystem prefix stays unproven.

name: maybe_Os_ScanParamBlocks
summary: Fallback scan of sixteen 0x40-byte blocks from offset 0x400 via Os_ReadChunkedTable: finds the word whose low byte is 0xFE with a matching checksum, unpacks two 12-bit fields plus two payload words into out, and returns 0xC8810FEF when nothing matches.
evidence: Os_ReadChunkedTable and the 0xC8810FEF SDK error code are solid, but the record owner is unnamed and both callers (maybe_Gfx_BlitWorker, maybe_Os_LookupParamEntry) are guesses, so what the scanned parameters describe stays open.

name: maybe_Container_RbTree_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a container owning a red-black tree plus a fixed 0x21-entry table: destroys the table, erases every tree node through the successor helpers, unlinks the object from its sibling list and frees it.
evidence: The std::map/set member is proven by std_RbTree_EraseNode / std__Rb_tree_rebalance / std_destroy_range on a 0x10-stride 0x21-entry table, but the owning class is unnamed and there are no callers, so only the generic Container_RbTree_Dtor name is honest.

name: Ui_Object_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a small UI object owning one smart handle: installs g_uiObjectBaseVtable, releases the handle at +0x10 through the handle-table validity test, unlinks the node from its sibling list and frees the block.
evidence: The installed base vtable is g_uiObjectBaseVtable and the teardown is the standard pair (Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry guarded by the 0x000FFFFF tag test, then Pack_ReleaseHandle, unlink and free), so both the family and the role are supported; there are no callers, which is normal for a destructor taken only from a vtable.

name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseMemberHandles4
summary: Releases the four generation-tagged handle members at +4, +0xC, +0x14 and +0x1C of the object whose base is self-0x1C and returns that base.
evidence: Four sibling Pack_ReleaseHandle calls at 8-byte strides returning self-4 - a template helper rather than a class member; the only caller Container_HashMap_Init does not name the owning structure.

name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseMemberHandles1
summary: Releases the single generation-tagged handle at +4 of the object whose base is self-4 and returns that base; the one-handle variant of 0x00120408.
evidence: Single Pack_ReleaseHandle call returning self-4, no callers and no class name; recorded as a template helper so a later pass can attach it to its struct.

name: maybe_Ui_DetachAndReleaseMembers
signature: int maybe_Ui_DetachAndReleaseMembers(void* self, u32 value, DetachTarget* target)
summary: Stores the value into target+8 and then releases the three generation-tagged handle members at self+0x14, +0xC and +4, returning self.
evidence: Three sibling Pack_ReleaseHandle calls at 8-byte strides plus the target+8 store; the callers Ui_Layout_UpdateScreenBuffers and maybe_Ui_MapWindow_ResolveTouchTarget place it in UI layout, but the detach noun is inferred from the store alone.

name: Ui_ItemInfoWindow_SubDtor
summary: Destructor of an item-info-window sub-object: installs g_uiItemInfoWindowObjectVtable, deletes the owned object at +0x13C through its vtable, releases the handle at +0x138, tears down the embedded 0x128-byte sub-object and frees the block.
evidence: The installed vtable is g_uiItemInfoWindowObjectVtable and the teardown (owned-object delete, Pack_ReleaseHandle, the 0x128-byte sub-object destructor 0x0021DD60, operator delete) is consistent; the vtable address, not the address neighbourhood, is what carries the class.

name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseMemberHandles2
summary: Releases the two generation-tagged handles at self-8 and self-4 and returns the base self-0xC.
evidence: Two Pack_ReleaseHandle calls and the returned base - no callers, no strings, no vtable, and the function is only reachable through a data pointer, so the owner type is unknowable here.

name: Data_BuildResourceDescriptorRecord
signature: void Data_BuildResourceDescriptorRecord(u32* out, u32 first, u32 second)
summary: Builds a 0x44-byte resource descriptor: formats the two ids through the enemy 2D-animation pack path descriptor into a 0x44-byte string buffer, copies the 17 words into out and overwrites out[0] with the shared-animation resource type tag.
evidence: The format descriptor is g_enemyAnim2dPackPathDesc and out[0] is replaced by g_sharedAnimationResourceTable, so the result is a {type tag, formatted path} resource descriptor; the three callers (BattleScene_BindUnitModelResources, Battle_Ui_LoadPartyModelResources, BattleScene_SyncUnitRenderResources) all bind unit model resources. The old TaggedRecord44 wording described the size, not the meaning.

name: maybe_SaveWork_IncrementIndexedCounter
summary: Increments the per-index u32 counter at (work+0x24A98)+0x2998+index*4 unless event-mode bit 0x80 is set and the current state value is at most 0xE; the callers are casino payout/slot screens and party-panel steps.
evidence: The guard reads work byte +0x2A474 bit 0x80 and func_0066B17C(bag, 0x15) > 0xE before func_006138D4(bag, index), so the increment of an indexed save counter is clear; which counter (casino payout history?) is not, and three of the six callers are only maybe_ named.

name: Battle_ClearActionSlots
summary: Resets the four 0x58-byte slot records at self+0x150 (zeroing the id/flag words and the 0x38-byte tail) and then refills one slot per active party member through Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionSlots.
evidence: Caller Battle_FinishCommandPhase calls it between rounds, the four-slot reset is fully readable and the refill uses the named Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionSlots on one slot per party list node, which fixes both the count and the role.

name: Battle_Ui_Step_DispatchFinishCommand
signature: int Battle_Ui_Step_DispatchFinishCommand(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Battle-UI sequence step: the +0x125C countdown gates a poll of the child widget, then it sends command 0x79 through Model_SetSlotState, sets the done byte +0xD2 and returns 1.
evidence: The +0x125C countdown / +0xD2 done-byte pattern and the Model_SetSlotState(..., 0x79, 1) call are explicit and match the other battle-UI steps in the 0x004ECxxx block; only the exact step number is inferred.

name: maybe_SlotTable_CommitAndRetire
signature: void maybe_SlotTable_CommitAndRetire(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Commits the 0x50-slot table: clears the bookkeeping words, copies 0x2C8-byte rows from f_E8 to f_EC, resets the copied source rows to sentinels and retires rows whose member state is 5 or 7/8.
evidence: The 1964-byte body keeps the same 0x2C8/0x8C row layout as the field slot table 0x00174E40, but its only caller (maybe_Menu_SumPartyStats) is itself maybe_ named and nothing names the table, so the commit/retire wording stays a description of the mechanism only.

name: Actor_UpdateAnimState
signature: u32 Actor_UpdateAnimState(int* self, u32 arg2, int whether)
summary: Steps the actor animation state machine for state ids 0x5C/0x5D: switches between them depending on frame vs half-clip and frame > 1, otherwise resets the animation through the vtable slots; returns 1, 2 or 3.
evidence: Body is intact apart from the float casts: the 0.5f frame/half-clip comparison, the state writes through vtable +0x124 and the returned phase 1/2/3 are all readable, and the same state pair is used by 0x001CCC0C which classifies the phase.

name: Actor_ClassifyAnimState
summary: Classifies the actor's animation phase: 2 when in state 0x5C with the frame at least half the clip, 3 when in state 0x5D with frame > 1, otherwise 1.
evidence: The three-way classification is fully readable and returns exactly the values 0x001CDC48 consumes, so the pair is a classify/apply state machine; the only missing piece is a caller for this half.

name: maybe_Actor_IsActiveState
summary: Composite activity predicate over three virtual queries (+0x10, +0x14, +0xD8) plus the type tests for ids 10 and 8.
evidence: The vtable slots are not named and the two type ids are unlabelled, so although the OR-chain returns a predicate value, what 'active' means here (visible? alive? queued?) is not verifiable and no caller confirms it.

name: maybe_FieldParty_UpdateSlotTypeFlags
summary: Loops the group members and their 7 slots, storing per-slot type-acceptance flags at group+0x1F2 and marking each slot used through the member's vtable +0x120.
evidence: The 7-slot loop, the Ui_TextLayout_IsTypeAccepted test (whose text name is clearly a misnomer here) and the vtable +0x120 call are readable, but the base register unaff_r6 = group+0x400 is lost so the offsets are approximate and no caller confirms the group class.

name: maybe_Menu_FindActorInListByType
summary: Walks an intrusive list and returns 1 when an entry reports type 0x9C.
evidence: The Thumb body is damaged: unaff_r4/unaff_r5 unresolved, a bogus arg1*0x2002 product and 1236 bytes of which only the 0x9C type test is attributable, and both callers are maybe_Menu_*. Nothing better than the current guess can be written.

name: maybe_Battle_Actor_CompareConditionFlags
signature: int maybe_Battle_Actor_CompareConditionFlags(void* actorA, void* actorB, unsigned int mask)
summary: Comparator over two battle actors using the isPartyMember byte and the type-10 condition value masked by the caller's mask; returns 0 or 1 depending on which side matches.
evidence: The four symmetric branches over isPartyMember and (type-10 value & mask) are visible and the body is intact, but with no caller and no vtable slot it cannot be told whether this is a sort predicate, a target filter or a can-act test; only CompareConditionFlags as a neutral description is safe.

name: Battle_Ui_WaitForCondition79
summary: Battle-UI sequence step waiting on a child widget and on unit kind 0x79: slot 1 of the battle-UI party-screen method table, with the +0x125C countdown and the +0xD2 done byte.
evidence: It is vtable slot 1 of the battle-UI party-screen table (slot 2 is Battle_Ui_Update) and the body is exactly the countdown / done-byte / type-0x79 wait pattern shared with 0x004ECDF0; only the step number is inferred from the constant.

name: maybe_Script_SqValueList_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a refcounted Squirrel value-array holder: installs vtable 0x007589F4, unlinks from its owner, releases the refcounted block at +0x1C, resets the 8-byte elements to the shared null value, destroys the element array with std_destroy_range and finally installs the base vtable 0x0075A728.
evidence: The structure (vtable 0x007589F4, refcount decrement at +4, std_destroy_range with 0x001BF798, base vtable 0x0075A728, g_sqNullObject) matches a refcounted value list, but the decompilation is damaged (unaff_r7, flag registers), so the name stays maybe_ at low confidence.

name: maybe_Object_ReleaseRefcountedChildren
summary: Damaged Thumb body (4400 bytes): refcount decrements followed by virtual slot +8 calls appear, but the control flow is unreliable.
evidence: Ghidra reports bad instruction data, unaff_/in_ registers and halt_baddata, and the three callers are Squirrel VM functions (Sq_VmInvokeDefaultToString, Script_Vm_CheckStackIndex, maybe_Script_VM_RunClosure) that do not fit a refcounted teardown, so the current name is a placeholder only.

name: maybe_Ui_CellGrid_InitSlots
summary: Initialises the 16 display cell slots at +0x8BC4 (0xB8 stride) from a zeroed 0x84-byte template with the default zero vectors and the 0xFF sentinel.
evidence: The 16-iteration loop copying a 0x84-byte template is explicit and the only caller is Ui_StatusWindow_RebuildSceneObjects, but the owning structure is only inferred and the CellGrid noun comes from the 0xB8 record layout alone.

name: maybe_Ui_CellGrid_CopySlots
summary: Copies the 0x2E-word slot records from +0x8C7C down to +0x8BC4 and stores the incoming 0x2E-word record at +0x923C; the same record layout as the cell-slot initialiser 0x001932D0.
evidence: The copy loop and the identical record layout to 0x001932D0 are certain, but the only caller Field_SceneObject_RegisterInstance does not identify the 0x8BC4 structure and no strings exist, so CellGrid stays a guess.

name: maybe_SceneObject_DeepCopy
signature: void maybe_SceneObject_DeepCopy(void* dst, const void* src, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Deep-copies a large (~0x450-byte) object: the 0x140-byte run, a 0x1E-word table, an 8x4 and a 0x68x2 element range plus 0xA0 bytes of auxiliary data, then fixes up the self-relative pointers.
evidence: The structure of the copy (std_memcpy of the fixed runs plus two std_uninitialized_copy element ranges) is clear and 14 named callers use it to duplicate actor/animation/battle-scene records, but which exact record type it copies is not visible, so the SceneObject noun stays generic.

name: maybe_Text_InitLineCache
signature: void maybe_Text_InitLineCache(TextLine* lines, const TextLine* source)
summary: Clears the 255 0x18-byte line records and then copies the first 0x11 bytes of each from the source template, re-initialising a message-line cache.
evidence: Two 0xFF-iteration loops with a 0x11-byte std_memcpy each are unambiguous, but both callers are maybe_ named (maybe_Ui_ResetLargeScreenState, maybe_Text_MeasureOverflow) and the record purpose is inferred from the 0x18 stride only. This is not item code.

name: maybe_Ui_ListData_RemoveSlot
summary: Removes one entry of a 19-slot table of 0x98-byte records: memmoves the following (0x13-index) records down one slot and clears the trailing 0x84-byte block plus the four header words at +0xB48..+0xBD9.
evidence: The shift is 0x98-byte records over 0x13 = 19 slots, which is not the party roster (FACTS: PartyMember is 0x12EC bytes x31). The companion 0x0018D3D4 is called with g_uiListData+0x6B8 and an id list by 0x003BDF58, so this is the UI list-data table, not the party - the old Party_RemoveMember name named the wrong owner.

name: maybe_Text_DecodeName
summary: Copies a 0x84-byte record, runs it through the layout builder 0x0018CEA4 and returns the two resulting bytes in out[0]/out[1].
evidence: The 0x84-byte record and the two result bytes are certain, but the layout helper is itself maybe_ named and the callers (PartyStatus_LoadNewestRecord, Ui_EquipWindow_InitMemberTables) do not say what the two bytes measure; DecodeName stays a guess. Not item code.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SetControlState
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_SetControlState(void* self, unsigned int state, unsigned char state2, void* out)
summary: Applies a text control-code state to a window part: stores the state byte at out+0x130 and self+8 and, unless the part is already fully initialised (state 8), copies the 0x48-byte g_uiWindowStateTransitionCallbacks table and installs the handler and its argument.
evidence: The only caller is the named Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyControlCode, which applies text control codes to a window part, and the copied table is g_uiWindowStateTransitionCallbacks - so this is window-state/handler installation, not an equipment part as the old name said. The part class is still open.

name: Ui_ListRow_InitFromRecord
summary: Initialises a list row from a record: sets the u16 id to 0xFFFF, the byte +6 to 0xFF and the word +8, copies the 0x29-byte record as the row name and maps record[0] to a row kind (0 -> 7, 1 -> 8, 2 -> 9).
evidence: The u16 0xFFFF / u8 0xFF / u32 id header plus the 0x29-byte name copy and the kind mapping are explicit, and the callers (Field_Gimmick_ActivateComponent1D8, maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_Ctor1) do not support the DungeonWindow noun that the old name claimed; the record layout is a plain list row.

name: maybe_Gfx_SkeletalAnim_InitFrame
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SkeletalAnim_InitFrame(int self, unsigned char* frame)
summary: Initialises per-frame animation work: copies a 0x120-byte default table and chooses the node-group offsets by frame kind (5/6) and flag bits.
evidence: Only std_memcpy is a named callee; there are no callers and the skeletal-animation context comes purely from the neighbouring animation vtables, so the class and the frame noun are unconfirmed.

name: Gfx_CopyBlock24
signature: void* Gfx_CopyBlock24(const void* src, void* dst)
summary: Copies one 24-byte record from src to dst and returns dst+0x18 so callers can chain the next record.
evidence: The body is exactly std_memcpy(dst, src, 0x18) followed by a return of dst+0x18, and the only caller Ui_LayoutText_SetupMaterialAndShading uses it to copy material records; the name is a literal description of a fully visible body.

name: Gfx_CopyBlock48
signature: void* Gfx_CopyBlock48(const void* src, void* dst)
summary: Copies one 48-byte record from src to dst and returns dst+0x30 so callers can chain the next record.
evidence: Same shape as 0x00558670 with a 0x30 size and a dst+0x30 return; the body is fully visible and the only doubt is the (unproven) graphics caller family.

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushStateBlockData
signature: int Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushStateBlockData(unsigned int* out, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int flags, GfxCmdBuf* self)
summary: Clears the dirty counters of a command-buffer object and, unless bit 0 of the flags is set, copies the stored command block to out and returns the 4-byte-aligned end pointer.
evidence: The body clears the five dirty counters and then does the conditional std_memcpy(out, self->commandQueue, commandCount) with an aligned end pointer, which is exactly the flush-to-out contract; it shares its instruction sequence with Gfx_CmdBuf_FlushStateBlock (0x558E4C), only taking the object in the 4th argument.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteColorBlock
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteColorBlock(void* self, GfxCmdBuf* cmd, unsigned int listIndex, unsigned int entryIndex)
summary: Writes one PICA command group for a 0x218-byte record: the flag word plus 24-bit colour, a second command header and, when the record is enabled, a 0x210-byte payload copy, advancing the command pointer.
evidence: The two command headers (0x000500E0, 0x000F00E1), the 0x218 stride and the 0x210 payload are explicit and the only caller is Gfx_CharShadow_BuildCurveTable, but what the 0x218-byte records hold (colours? materials?) is not visible, so ColorBlock stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_SetTextRow
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DataPanel_SetTextRow(WorkData* self, const void* src)
summary: Copies a 0x84-byte row block into self+0x86B4 and then processes the name at +0x86C2 (wcsncpy / wcslen).
evidence: Eighteen callers (AddCasinoCoinNum, Field_SetFlagBit, ATMCoin, Ui_PokerWindow_Payout, Ui_JackpotScreen_EndPayout, Casino_Slot_PlaceBet, ...) all push a 0x84-byte row into the same work block, so the receiver is the game work status/text panel; the visible body is truncated after the row copy and the wcslen call, so the panel noun stays maybe_. This is not item code - the name only describes a text row.

name: maybe_GameWork_RemoveActiveRecord
signature: void maybe_GameWork_RemoveActiveRecord(int work, int index, int count)
summary: Removes one entry from the 0x14-slot index table at work+0x5FE4 by memmoving the following 0x8C-byte records down, then clears the 0x84-byte tail at +0x7AB0 and resets +0x7B34/+0x7B35/+0x7B38.
evidence: The memmove over 0x8C-byte records with a 0x14-byte index slot and the trailing flag reset are readable, but the only caller is maybe_Ui_ListWindow_AdvancePage5 and the table owner is still inferred, so active-record wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_CopyBlocks
summary: Copies a run of 0x200-byte command-buffer blocks: per block the 0x1FC-byte payload plus a header word, then a final partial block whose size is packed into the 0xFFF00000 mask.
evidence: The block copy and the size-mask packing are recognisable, but the body uses 22 unaff_ values, ends in an indirect result and its only caller (maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_BindHandles) is unnamed, so even the Gfx subsystem is a guess.

name: maybe_Party_ShiftRecordSlots
summary: Inserts a 0x44-byte record into the five-slot array at +0x92F4 (or appends it at +0x9404 through Text_StyleList_Insert) after the id-validity check on the first slot.
evidence: The 0x44-byte slots between +0x92F4 and +0x9448 and the 0xFF-added id test are visible, but the shift count is a damaged magic multiply (0x78787879) and the wcslen call 0x00100B74 is mis-marked noreturn, so the slot logic cannot be verified.

name: Ui_Window_OnInputSelectEntry
summary: Window input handler for the select-entry input: dispatches the panel's f_3C handler, takes the selected entry's action-node id, runs ActorActionSeq_RunNode on it, refreshes the status text and the number field and pushes the animator to state 7 or 1.
evidence: The body is readable and structurally identical to the other window input handlers in this batch (input mask 0x142/4/0x10/1 on f_3534), with the named ActorActionSeq_RunNode, Ui_MessageWindow_SetStatusTextByType and Ui_SetNumberTextValue calls; the select branch is the one that reads the list's selected entry.

name: Ui_ScriptedScreen_HandleInput
summary: Input handler of a script-driven screen: lazily creates its 0x98-byte resource-node helper, polls it, and then dispatches the screen's input bits (0x142/4/8/0x10/1) to the animator states, the scripted-element activation, the text owner and the action-node runner.
evidence: Same input-bit dispatch as the other Ui_Window_OnInput* handlers in this batch and it calls the now-supported Ui_ActivateScriptedElement for bit 8; the extra lazy 0x98-byte Engine_ResourceNode helper is what makes this a scripted screen rather than a plain list window.

name: Ui_Window_OnInputRunActionNodeB
summary: Second input handler that runs action nodes: input bit 4 pushes animator state 0xC, bit 8 activates the scripted element, bit 0x10 sets the list-item flag, otherwise it runs the selected node's action and refreshes the list row colour.
evidence: Readable body with the same 0x142/4/8/0x10/1 dispatch as its siblings; this one differs by animator state 0xC and by the Ui_ListRow_ApplyValueColor refresh after the action run.

name: Ui_Window_OnInputConfirm
summary: Confirm input handler of a script-driven window: runs the selected action node with the confirm flag (1), advances the animator to state 0x19 in the active-node branch and sets the window's action-started flag.
evidence: Its body is the confirm half of 0x002A5FD4 (identical structure, ActorActionSeq_RunNode called with flag 1 and animator state 0x19 instead of 0/2), which fixes both the pair and the role; named callees are ActorActionSeq_RunNode and func_003BDD90.

name: Ui_Window_OnInputCancel
summary: Cancel input handler of the same window: runs the selected action node with the cancel flag (0), activates the scripted element on bit 8 and advances the animator to state 2 in the active-node branch.
evidence: Exact mirror of 0x002A5E4C with flag 0, animator state 2 and the extra bit-8 branch to Ui_ActivateScriptedElement, so the confirm/cancel pairing is established.

name: Ui_Window_OnInputRunActionNode
summary: Input handler that runs the selected action node: bit 4 pushes animator state 0, bit 8 activates the scripted element, bit 0x10 sets the list-item flag, otherwise it runs the node action (animator states 0x13/0x14/0x15/0x16 depending on the node flags).
evidence: Same 0x142/4/8/0x10/1 dispatch as the sibling handlers with readable animator state ids and the named ActorActionSeq_RunNode; its distinguishing feature is the four-way animator state choice in the node branch.

name: Ui_Window_StepSelectListRow
summary: Input/step handler that acts on the selected list row: bit 4 pushes animator state 0x12, bit 0x10 sets the list-item flag, otherwise it takes the row id from the list object (func_0064E31C) and runs that action node.
evidence: Readable body of the same input-handler family, but the node id comes from the list object at bufferAB8 rather than from the pane, which is what the StepSelectListRow wording describes; the row lookups func_0064E31C/func_0064E2F4 are unnamed but consistent.

name: Ui_Window_OnInputRunSubPaneActionNode
summary: Window input handler variant: bit 4 pushes animator state 0xE, bit 8 activates the scripted element, bit 0x10 sets the list-item flag, otherwise it runs the sub-pane's action node (and, when the node's +0x14 flag is set, also func_003BDD90 and animator state 0xD).
evidence: Structurally identical to Ui_Window_OnInputRunActionNode (0x002A66EC) but with animator states 0xE/0xD and the extra node flag test; the old RunCommon3 name said nothing about it.

name: maybe_Ui_ActionWindow_InitSlots
summary: Initialises the six-entry action list of a scripted window: pushes vtable slot +0x54 with 0x2F, sets the list count, builds the list entries (Ui_ListData_BuildEntries(.., 6, -1, 0)), marks the flag block and fills each slot with 0xFFFFFFFF and the five Flag_GetGlobalIndexed defaults.
evidence: The six-slot loop, Ui_ListData_BuildEntries(..., 6, -1, 0) and the five Flag_GetGlobalIndexed reads are readable, but the body is otherwise damaged (one indirect call goes through an unresolved slot) and no caller names the window, so the ActionWindow noun stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithBalloon
summary: Closes a message-window variant: finishes the transition of the record at *(self+0xB0)+0x146 and releases the attached widget at self+0x84.
evidence: The two calls (Ui_SmithMenu_FinishTransition on the +0xB0 record and Ui_Window_ReleaseAttached on self+0x84) are clear, but nothing identifies the attached widget as a balloon and there are no callers, so the WithBalloon wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorWithChildren
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorWithChildren(u32 owner, int descriptor, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Factory-table constructor: creates a 0x4000000C-tagged object through 0x0028E630, installs g_uiSlotWidgetVtable plus its secondary table at +0x98, sets the 0xFFFF/0xFF sentinels and default-constructs four 0x48-byte handle-ref children.
evidence: The construction shape matches the other 0x0028E630-based ctors (Field_Gadget_Ctor, Field_DragController_Ctor, Actor2D_ShadowNode_Ctor) but the installed vtable is g_uiSlotWidgetVtable, i.e. a UI slot widget with four handle-ref children, so the Field_SceneObject noun is doubtful and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_Ctor
signature: FieldGadget* maybe_Field_Gadget_Ctor(u32 owner, int model_id, u32 record, u32 flags)
summary: Constructor of a field object with an embedded handle reference: allocates through 0x0028E630 with the 0x4000000C tag, installs g_fieldGadgetComponentVtable at +0x22C plus its sub-vtable, constructs the Actor_HandleRef at +0x298 and seeds the id/layer words.
evidence: Allocation, the vtable at +0x22C and the Actor_HandleRef_Ctor at +0x298 are verified and the installed global is g_fieldGadgetComponentVtable, but there is no caller and no string that names the class as a gadget, so maybe_ stays.
